description:
A reusable pipeline that turns completed cells in any published-format campaign dataset into estimate tables with interval columns, zero-fraction curves against matrix size, and comparison columns against published prior art, while retaining halted cells' partial raw counts and reasons without synthesizing estimates or verdicts.

## Background

The repository already carries a permanent-domain plot generator and a set of reproduction wrappers for this problem family, so figure generation has a precedent to sit beside rather than a convention to invent. What it must add is the discipline the repository requires of every Monte Carlo artefact: each estimate states its sample count and interval, and every plot or table carries error bars or interval columns.

The comparison against published $q = 3$ numerics is a first-class output rather than a remark. The right comparison is achieved precision, not trial count: matching the published sample sizes is not a goal, resolving $\delta(n) = p(n) - 1/q$ is. The published table gives point estimates without uncertainty, so supplying uncertainty metadata for every published-source cell — exact/no-sampling-uncertainty bounds for exact rows and, by reanalysis, Wilson intervals for Monte Carlo counts — is a contribution independent of how many samples any campaign draws.

This is tooling. It is developed and tested against fixture datasets in the published format, so its correctness does not wait on a campaign finishing, and it can be re-run against any later campaign.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The pipeline reads a dataset in the campaign's published format and emits the pooled sample count, point estimate $\hat p$, and $95\%$ Wilson interval for each completed $(q,n)$; a halted row emits its pooled raw counts and reason with no estimate, interval, or verdict.
- [hard] REQ-02: Curves of completed-cell $\hat p$ against $n$ per field carry interval error bars, and no emitted figure or table states an estimate without its sample count and its interval.
- [hard] REQ-03: Comparison columns for a completed cell against published $q = 3$ counts carry the published point estimate, the source row's exact/no-sampling-uncertainty representation or Wilson interval obtained by reanalysis of its Monte Carlo counts, the dataset's own interval, and a precision classification. A halted counterpart carries raw counts and reason but no estimate-based comparison.
- [hard] REQ-04: A completed cell whose interval excludes a published point estimate is flagged in the output rather than smoothed over.
- [hard] REQ-05: The pipeline refuses a dataset whose checksums do not verify, and refuses a dataset whose cells lack terminal states, rather than plotting from a tree it cannot vouch for.
- [hard] REQ-06: The pipeline runs from the dataset alone with no value transcribed by hand, and rerunning it against an unchanged dataset reproduces byte-identical outputs.
- [hard] REQ-07: Emitted figures and tables carry no interpretive text, so the wording of conclusions lives in an analysis narrative rather than in generated artefacts.
- [hard] REQ-08: Committed fixture datasets in the published format, including one with a halted cell and one with a checksum mismatch, exercise the pipeline's outputs and its refusals in an automated test.

## Notes

Outputs are keyed by campaign id so results from two campaigns never overwrite one another.
title: Curve and table generation pipeline
